With 8 of us alive — Alice, Bob, Carol, Grace, Heidi, Ivan, Judy, and me — the Village wins once all Yakuza and the SK are eliminated, but I still don't know how many Yakuza remain among the group. A Standard shot can kill Defense None or Basic targets, while a Strong shot is needed to pierce the SK's Standard defense, so my choice of weapon strength tonight matters as much as my choice of target.

Heidi's Diviner claim stands out, especially given the heavy PM traffic between her and Judy around Day 4 and both of them pushing guilty votes on Erin and Mallory. I'm also weighing Alice's Trapper claim against Niaj's tracking report that Alice visited Heidi, which Niaj flagged as unverified — if the trap was real and armed on Heidi, the lack of any trap reports since suggests no non-Village actor has visited her.

Tracing the deaths: Niaj fell N3 to the Katana-wielder plus the SK, Frank died N2 after tracking that he'd visited Alice and Mallory as part of his Seer role. None of this cleanly points to the killer, so I'm considering Carol instead — her fast nomination of Erin while claiming Coroner makes her a plausible Yakuza liar worth targeting with the shot.

Alternatively, if Carol's claim is genuine — her exam matching Frank's true Seer role and flagging Erin as non-Good — then Erin likely was the Serial Killer all along, having attacked both Frank and Niaj before being hanged, which would mean no SK remains active and the ledger of deaths lines up cleanly with Katana-plus-SK.

That leaves lingering uncertainty about remaining Yakuza, since Erin might instead have been a Wiretap-aligned Yakuza rather than the SK, and no other evidence clearly identifies the real killer among Judy, Heidi, Bob, Carol, or Grace's claims. Given the lack of concrete leads and the risk of hitting a Good player with a blind shot, I'm leaning toward holding my action this night, saving the shot for a clearer target rather than gambling on roughly a third chance of hitting Yakuza.

No concrete lead on a Defense None Yakuza, and a Basic shot on a Good player would be costly, so I hold my tokens.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9); a role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Cardinal who died today or dies tonight: code deals their Divine Attack on a random Good player after your resolution, at the end of the night. Don't draw or kill a victim yourself.
- A Coroner who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the examine op, which spends the token; code tells them the role and tokens left. Don't tell() the Coroner anything about it. The target must have died before the night began. It is an Astral Visit, not a visit (R6): nothing that reacts to visits sees it.
- A Diviner who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the divine op; code draws the role and tells them. Don't tell() the Diviner anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. If they picked a Yakuza, don't use the op: that player has Strong Defense tonight, and the Diviner gets no result.
- Jester revenge attacks are carried out by code after you finish; don't resolve them.
- A Juror who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) and named two different players other than themselves (target and second_target; dead players allowed): use the jury op with those two players; code tells the Juror the result. Don't tell() the Juror anything about it. It is an Astral Visit, so it visits no one.
- A Profiler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the profile op, which spends the token; code tells them the result and tokens left. Don't tell() the Profiler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Puppeteer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the puppet op, which spends the token; code swaps who chats tomorrow.
- The Seer learns about two random players other than themself each night (random_choice) from those alive when the night began, including anyone who died that night (rules R10), unless they spent a token to choose them. A chosen pair visits both players; the random pair isn't a visit. A role-blocked Seer gets no pair at all.
- Trapper traps persist across nights: set_status key 'trapped_by' to the Trapper's name on the trapped player, and set it to null when the trap is used up, replaced or removed (a Trapper removes it by acting with no target). Trapping the player the trap is already on isn't allowed: it has no effect and the trap stays armed. If several non-Village players visit a trapped player the same night, random_choice picks the one hit.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9); a role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Cardinal who died today or dies tonight: code deals their Divine Attack on a random Good player after your resolution, at the end of the night. Don't draw or kill a victim yourself.
- A Coroner who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the examine op, which spends the token; code tells them the role and tokens left. Don't tell() the Coroner anything about it. The target must have died before the night began. It is an Astral Visit, not a visit (R6): nothing that reacts to visits sees it.
- A Diviner who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the divine op; code draws the role and tells them. Don't tell() the Diviner anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. If they picked a Yakuza, don't use the op: that player has Strong Defense tonight, and the Diviner gets no result.
- Jester revenge attacks are carried out by code after you finish; don't resolve them.
- A Juror who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) and named two different players other than themselves (target and second_target; dead players allowed): use the jury op with those two players; code tells the Juror the result. Don't tell() the Juror anything about it. It is an Astral Visit, so it visits no one.
- A Profiler who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the profile op, which spends the token; code tells them the result and tokens left. Don't tell() the Profiler anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Puppeteer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the puppet op, which spends the token; code swaps who chats tomorrow.
- The Seer learns about two random players other than themself each night (random_choice) from those alive when the night began, including anyone who died that night (rules R10), unless they spent a token to choose them. A chosen pair visits both players; the random pair isn't a visit. A role-blocked Seer gets no pair at all.
- Trapper traps persist across nights: set_status key 'trapped_by' to the Trapper's name on the trapped player, and set it to null when the trap is used up, replaced or removed (a Trapper removes it by acting with no target). Trapping the player the trap is already on isn't allowed: it has no effect and the trap stays armed. If several non-Village players visit a trapped player the same night, random_choice picks the one hit.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.

Review: low, player confusionIvan and Bob (Day 4) argued that because Bob claims Juror, Erin's profile (Juror/Serial Killer/Wiretap) can't be Juror. The setup says roles may repeat except unique ones (Smuggler, Vulture), so Bob's claim doesn't rule out Erin being a Juror.
Review: low, player confusionMallory's Day 3 claim said 'Day 2: No on Frank's nomination (I nominated him)'. The nominator votes Yes by default, and the log shows Mallory voted Yes. The claim contradicts itself and is false (possibly a Jester bluff, but it reads like confusion about the nominator's default vote).
Review: low, prompt problemThe claim ledger cuts claims at 40 words (Bob's was cut twice). Grace and Frank said in the debrief that this hid part of Bob's vote history, which made checking votes harder.
Review: low, harness bugPlayers hit output-format friction: Ivan's StructuredOutput failed to parse when he wrote unquoted nulls inside a raw JSON string; Dave had to fill every required field with placeholders (claim, last will); Heidi found that names in quotes were rejected in the Katana vote fields. The schema should accept empty or optional fields and normalize name strings.
Game over
WinnersAlice, Bob, Carol, Frank, Grace, Ivan, Niaj, Olivia, Mallory
